claim: The hunchback P2 (HbP2) enhancer drives a sharp expression pattern in the Drosophila blastoderm embryo in response to the transcriptional activator Bicoid (Bcd).
source: Here we examine the hunchback P2 (HbP2) enhancer which drives a sharp expression pattern in the Drosophila blastoderm embryo in response to the transcriptional activator Bicoid (Bcd).
evidence: This is a direct statement from the abstract describing the experimental system studied.

claim: The prevailing model based on pairwise cooperative binding of Bcd to HbP2 is not adequate to explain the sharp expression pattern.
source: We systematically interrogate cis and trans factors that influence the shape and position of expression driven by HbP2, and find that the prevailing model, based on pairwise cooperative binding of Bcd to HbP2 is not adequate.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract based on systematic experimental interrogation.

claim: Other proteins such as pioneer factors, Mediator and histone modifiers influence the shape and position of the HbP2 expression pattern.
source: We demonstrate that other proteins, such as pioneer factors, Mediator and histone modifiers influence the shape and position of the HbP2 expression pattern.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract based on experimental perturbations.

claim: Higher-order cooperativity and energy expenditure impact boundary location and sharpness of the HbP2 expression pattern.
source: Comparing our results to theory reveals how higher-order cooperativity and energy expenditure impact boundary location and sharpness.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from comparing experimental results to theoretical predictions.

claim: The bacterial view of transcription regulation, where pairwise interactions between regulatory proteins dominate, must be reexamined in animals.
source: Our results emphasize that the bacterial view of transcription regulation, where pairwise interactions between regulatory proteins dominate, must be reexamined in animals, where multiple molecular mechanisms collaborate to shape the gene regulatory function.
evidence: This is a broad conclusion drawn from the experimental findings and theoretical analysis.

claim: The hunchback gene has three enhancers that drive anterior expression: HbP2, a distal shadow enhancer, and a distal stripe enhancer.
source: The anterior expression of hb is set by three enhancers: HbP2, which is promoter-proximal, a distal shadow enhancer and a distal stripe enhancer (Figure 1).
evidence: This is stated in the text and illustrated in Figure 1, citing previous work (Perry et al., 2012; Perry et al., 2011).

claim: HbP2 drives early expression of hb at nuclear cycle 14, while the shadow enhancer and stripe enhancer contribute to expression at later times.
source: HbP2 drives early expression of hb at nuclear cycle 14, while the shadow enhancer and stripe enhancer contribute to expression at later times (Perry et al., 2012; Perry et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the text with citations to previous work.

claim: The Hill coefficient for endogenous hb mRNA expression pattern is 6.2 +/- 1.1.
source: We measure a Hill coefficient for the endogenous hb mRNA expression pattern of 6.2 +/- 1.1, which corresponds with other reports in the literature (Gregor et al., 2007; He et al., 2011; Lopes et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from the study with citations to corroborating literature.

claim: The Hill coefficient for WTHbP2 is 5.2+/- 0.3.
source: For WTHbP2, the Hill coefficient is 5.2+/- 0.3, indicating that HbP2 enhancer alone can drive sharp expression comparable to expression from native hb locus.
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from the study.

claim: HbP2 enhancer alone can drive sharp expression comparable to expression from native hb locus.
source: For WTHbP2, the Hill coefficient is 5.2+/- 0.3, indicating that HbP2 enhancer alone can drive sharp expression comparable to expression from native hb locus.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the Hill coefficient measurement.

claim: A common assumption is that Bcd binds cooperatively to 6 Bcd binding sites in HbP2 and that this gives rise to a Hill coefficient of ~6.
source: A common assumption based on Hill fits to the endogenous Hb mRNA pattern is that Bcd binds cooperatively to 6 Bcd binding sites in HbP2 and that this gives rise to a Hill coefficient of ~6; more generally this model states that cooperative binding at n sites gives rise to a Hill function with coefficient nH = n.
evidence: This describes a prevailing assumption in the field that the study tests.

claim: Removing all 6 Bcd binding sites from HbP2 does not abolish expression.
source: First, eliminating all 6 Bcd binding sites does not abolish expression.
evidence: This is an experimental observation from the binding site deletion series.

claim: Other binding sites, either for Bcd or other TFs, contribute to HbP2 expression.
source: This indicates that other binding sites, either for Bcd or other TFs, contribute to HbP2 expression, which has been previously argued in the literature (Chen et al., 2012; Holloway and Spirov, 2015; Liu and Ma, 2013; Mito et al., 2006; Xu et al., 2014).
evidence: This is an inference from the experimental observation that expression persists after removing all 6 canonical Bcd sites, supported by citations.

claim: The Hill coefficient decreases by ~0.5 for each Bcd site removed.
source: Second, while the Hill coefficient does decrease as Bcd sites are removed, it only decreases by ~0.5 for each site removed.
evidence: This is a quantitative observation from the binding site deletion series.

claim: Removing Bcd binding sites decreases the gMM constant and shifts the expression of HbP2 toward the anterior.
source: Removing Bcd binding sites also decreases the gMM constant and shifts the expression of HbP2 toward the anterior.
evidence: This is an experimental observation from the binding site deletion series.

claim: The assumption that Hill coefficient follows a one-to-one relationship with the number of binding sites in the enhancer is wrong.
source: Together, these results indicate that the assumption that Hill coefficient follows a one-to-one relationship with the number of binding sites in the enhancer is wrong, as we would have predicted from our biophysical model.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental observations and theoretical predictions.

claim: HbP2 contains three strong affinity Bcd binding sites (sTFBSs) and three weak affinity sites (wTFBSs).
source: Of the six Bicoid binding sites, three are strong affinity sites (sTFBSs) and three weak affinity sites (wTFBSs).
evidence: This is a description of the HbP2 sequence composition.

claim: All six Bcd binding sites contribute roughly equally to GRF shape, despite variations in affinity and position.
source: Together, these results indicate that all six binding sites contribute roughly equally to GRF shape, despite variations in affinity and position, which was also observed in other work (Smith, 2015).
evidence: This is a conclusion from experiments testing individual and clustered binding site deletions, supported by a citation.

claim: HbP2 contains predicted binding motifs for TFs other than Bcd, including Hb itself and the pioneer factor Zelda.
source: HbP2 contains predicted binding motifs for TFs other than Bcd, including Hb itself and the pioneer factor Zelda (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 3A.

claim: SynHbP2 maintains the endogenous Bcd binding sites in place but replaces the intervening sequences with computationally designed 'neutral sequences'.
source: This sequence maintains the endogenous Bcd binding sites in place but replaces the intervening sequences with computationally designed 'neutral sequences'; these neutral spacers are devoid of motifs for 11 TFs known to regulate even-skipped that are expressed in the blastoderm (Bcd, Cad, dStat, D, Gt, Hb, Kni, Kr, Nub, Tll, Zld) (Estrada et al., 2016a).
evidence: This describes the design of the synthetic enhancer construct.

claim: Robust expression from SynHbP2 requires 7 bp of endogenous sequence flanking each Bcd binding site.
source: Robust expression requires 7 bp of endogenous sequence flanking each Bcd binding site; using only the 7 bp core Bcd binding motif, or motifs flanked by 2 bp did not drive robust expression (Figure 3A, right).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from testing different SynHbP2 variants.

claim: SynHbP2 drives expression comparable to WTHbP2, with a similar Hill coefficient but at an anteriorly shifted location in the embryo.
source: SynHbP2 drives expression comparable to WTHbP2, with a similar Hill coefficient but at an anteriorly shifted location in the embryo, corresponding to an increased gMM constant (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is an experimental observation comparing SynHbP2 to WTHbP2.

claim: Bcd alone can mediate sharp expression.
source: These results indicate that Bcd alone can mediate sharp expression but that other TFs, such as Hb and Zelda may affect the gMM constant and the location of the GRF along the AP axis.
evidence: This is an inference from the SynHbP2 expression data.

claim: Other TFs, such as Hb and Zelda may affect the gMM constant and the location of the GRF along the AP axis.
source: These results indicate that Bcd alone can mediate sharp expression but that other TFs, such as Hb and Zelda may affect the gMM constant and the location of the GRF along the AP axis.
evidence: This is an inference from the anterior shift observed in SynHbP2 compared to WTHbP2.

claim: Knock-down of hb shifted the location of WTHbP2 expression by 8% anteriorly along the AP axis without distinctive changes in the steepness of the response (nH(hbRNAi)=5.9 ± 0.6).
source: Indeed, knock-down of hb and Zelda shifted the location of expression by 8% and 5% anteriorly along the AP axis without distinctive changes in the steepness of the response (nH(hbRNAi)=5.9 ± 0.6, nH(Zelda RNAi)=5.8 ± 0.9).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from RNAi experiments.

claim: Knock-down of Zelda shifted the location of WTHbP2 expression by 5% anteriorly along the AP axis without distinctive changes in the steepness of the response (nH(Zelda RNAi)=5.8 ± 0.9).
source: Indeed, knock-down of hb and Zelda shifted the location of expression by 8% and 5% anteriorly along the AP axis without distinctive changes in the steepness of the response (nH(hbRNAi)=5.9 ± 0.6, nH(Zelda RNAi)=5.8 ± 0.9).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from RNAi experiments.

claim: Previous studies have noted an anterior shift in HbP2 expression when Zelda or Hb are perturbed.
source: Previous studies have noted an anterior shift in HbP2 expression when Zelda or Hb are perturbed, although the GRF was not quantitatively analysed (Xu et al., 2014).
evidence: This cites previous work that observed similar effects.

claim: Knocking down CBP results in a distinctive shift in location of expression toward the anterior (34 ± 2.5 %AP) without much change to the Hill coefficient (nH = 4.5 ± 0.53).
source: Indeed, we found that knocking down CBP or HDAC6, both proteins involved in histone acetylation, results in a distinctive shift in location of expression toward the anterior (34 ± 2.5 %AP, 40 ± 1.5%AP respectively) without much change to the Hill coefficient (nH = 4.5 ± 0.53 and nH = 6.22 ± 0.03 respectively) (Figure 4, Table 1).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from RNAi experiments.

claim: Knocking down HDAC6 results in a distinctive shift in location of expression toward the anterior (40 ± 1.5%AP) without much change to the Hill coefficient (nH = 6.22 ± 0.03).
source: Indeed, we found that knocking down CBP or HDAC6, both proteins involved in histone acetylation, results in a distinctive shift in location of expression toward the anterior (34 ± 2.5 %AP, 40 ± 1.5%AP respectively) without much change to the Hill coefficient (nH = 4.5 ± 0.53 and nH = 6.22 ± 0.03 respectively) (Figure 4, Table 1).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from RNAi experiments.

claim: CBP is a histone acetyl transferase and the Drosophila ortholog of p300.
source: For example, Creb Binding Protein (CBP) a histone acetyl transferase and the Drosophila ortholog of p300 (Fu et al., 2004), is known to destabilize chromatin and facilitate chromatin opening (Chan and La Thangue, 2001).
evidence: This is stated with citations to previous work.

claim: CBP is known to destabilize chromatin and facilitate chromatin opening.
source: For example, Creb Binding Protein (CBP) a histone acetyl transferase and the Drosophila ortholog of p300 (Fu et al., 2004), is known to destabilize chromatin and facilitate chromatin opening (Chan and La Thangue, 2001).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to previous work.

claim: CBP is reported to be an enhancer-dependent co-activator of Bcd, facilitating its activation in S2 cells.
source: CBP is also reported to be an enhancer-dependent co-activator of Bcd, facilitating its activation in S2 cells (Fu et al., 2004).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to previous work.

claim: Knocking down Mediator subunits had three types of effects on the WTHbP2 GRF: some subunits reduce overall expression level, some affect the gMM constant but not the Hill coefficient, and some decrease the Hill coefficient but do not affect the gMM constant.
source: We found that knocking down Mediator subunits had three types of effects on the WTHbP2 GRF. First, some subunits, such as MED14, reduce the overall expression level. Second, some subunits, such as MED20 and MED22, do not affect the Hill coefficient, but do affect the gMM constant. Finally, some subunits, such as MED11 and MED27, decrease the Hill coefficient, but do not affect the gMM constant (Figure 5).
evidence: This summarizes experimental observations from RNAi experiments targeting different Mediator subunits.

claim: The WTHbP2 and SynHbP2 GRFs lie on the boundary of the position-steepness region predicted by the thermodynamic equilibrium model.
source: We find that the WTHbP2 and SynHbP2 GRFs lie on the boundary of the position-steepness region, and that pairwise cooperativities, either TF-TF or TF-Pol, are inadequate to explain the data.
evidence: This is a conclusion from comparing experimental data to theoretical predictions.

claim: Pairwise cooperativities, either TF-TF or TF-Pol, are inadequate to explain the WTHbP2 and SynHbP2 data.
source: We find that the WTHbP2 and SynHbP2 GRFs lie on the boundary of the position-steepness region, and that pairwise cooperativities, either TF-TF or TF-Pol, are inadequate to explain the data.
evidence: This is a conclusion from comparing experimental data to theoretical predictions.

claim: The deletion constructs yield GRFs whose steepness is higher than the thermodynamic equilibrium model can accommodate, especially for low numbers of TF binding sites.
source: Moreover, the deletion constructs yield GRFs whose steepness is higher than the model can accommodate, especially for low numbers of TF binding sites.
evidence: This is a conclusion from comparing experimental data from deletion constructs to theoretical predictions.

claim: The relationship between binding site number and Hill coefficient predicted by the classical model does not hold for HbP2.
source: We first demonstrate that predicted relationship between binding site number and Hill coefficient does not hold.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion stated in the Discussion based on the experimental results.

claim: Bcd, other TFs and co-factors such as Mediator and CBP work together to shape the GRF through two largely separable properties - the steepness and position of the response.
source: Then, we put forward data to support an alternative model where Bcd, other TFs and co-factors such as Mediator and CBP work together to shape the GRF through two largely separable properties - the steepness and position of the response.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion stated in the Discussion based on the experimental results.

claim: Either unrecognized Bcd binding sites contribute to HbP2 expression, or activation by a single TF at thermodynamic equilibrium may not be adequate to explain the response of HbP2.
source: Finally, by comparing our results to theory, we propose that either unrecognized Bcd binding sites contribute to HbP2 expression, or that activation by a single TF at thermodynamic equilibrium may not be adequate to explain the response of HbP2, even when accounting for higher order cooperativities between TFs.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion stated in the Discussion based on comparing experimental results to theory.

claim: Driever and Nusslein-Volhard's constructs differ from the current study in that they removed Bcd TFBS by truncating WTHbP2 to shorter pieces, which also removes other neighboring sequences and changes the distance of binding sites relative to the promoter.
source: Driever and Nusslein-Volhard removed Bcd TFBS by truncating WTHbP2 to shorter pieces. This strategy not only removes Bcd TFBS but also other neighboring sequences and it changes the distance of binding sites relative to the promoter.
evidence: This describes a methodological difference between the current study and previous work.

claim: The current study's series of HbP2 variants preserve enhancer length, binding site positions and inter-motif sequences.
source: In contrast, our series of HbP2 variants preserve enhancer length, binding site positions and inter-motif sequences.
evidence: This describes a methodological feature of the current study.

claim: The current study used the native Hb promoter rather than the HSP 70 promoter or a smaller fragment of the Hb promoter.
source: All of our reporters used the native Hb promoter (Perry et al., 2012) rather than using the HSP 70 promoter (Driever et al., 1989) or a smaller fragment of the Hb promoter (+1 to+107) (Driever et al., 1989).
evidence: This describes a methodological feature of the current study with citations to previous work.

claim: The current study used quantitative imaging methods to measure the output of HbP2 variants.
source: But most significantly, we used quantitative imaging methods to measure the output of our HbP2 variants; this allows us to interpret our data differently.
evidence: This describes a methodological feature of the current study.

claim: The Hill coefficient decreases by 0.5 with each Bcd site removed rather than by one as would be predicted by the classical model.
source: We find that the changes to the GRF upon binding site removal do not conform to the simple model where n binding sites can produce a GRF with a Hill coefficient of n. Instead, the Hill coefficient decreases by 0.5 with each site removed (rather than by one as would be predicted).
evidence: This is a quantitative observation from the binding site deletion experiments.

claim: Recent quantitative studies measured Hill coefficients between 5 and 6 for the Bcd/Hb GRF, largely agreeing with the current study.
source: Importantly, all of these studies, including ours, largely agree, measuring Hill coefficients between 5 and 6.
evidence: This compares the current study's results to previous quantitative studies.

claim: Endogenous hb mRNA cannot be directly interpreted as the output of the HbP2 GRF because it is difficult to exclude outputs from other hb enhancers.
source: However endogenous hb mRNA (and endogenous Hb protein) cannot be directly interpreted as the output of the HbP2 GRF because it is difficult to exclude outputs from other hb enhancers that are known to contribute to anterior hb gene expression (Perry et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a methodological consideration stated with a citation.

claim: A recent quantitative fluorescence in situ hybridization study showed evidence of ~6 Bicoid molecules bound to the hb locus of earlier stage embryos.
source: Lastly, we note that a recent quantitative fluorescence in situ hybridization study showed evidence of ~6 Bicoid molecules bound to the hb locus of earlier stage embryos (Xu et al., 2015).
evidence: This cites a previous study's finding.

claim: The current study's results suggest that either more than 6 Bcd molecules are interacting on HbP2, or energy is being spent to maintain the system away from equilibrium.
source: Our results suggest that either more than 6 Bcd molecules are interacting on HbP2, or energy is being spent to maintain the system away from equilibrium.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the current study's results in light of previous findings.

claim: In the current study using the endogenous enhancer in embryos, the arrangement, position, orientation, clustering and affinity of Bcd binding sites were not distinctive features for the degree of cooperativity.
source: In our study using the endogenous enhancer in embryos, the arrangement, position, orientation, clustering and affinity of Bcd binding sites were not distinctive features for the degree of cooperativity.
evidence: This is a conclusion from experiments testing different binding site configurations.

claim: Bcd belongs to the homeodomain protein family, which recognize a common -TAAT- motif.
source: Bcd belongs to the homeodomain protein family, which recognize a common -TAAT- motif.
evidence: This is established knowledge about Bcd.

claim: Bcd binds to the specific TAATCC motif.
source: While some homeodomain proteins have a degenerate specificity (Berger et al., 2008; Christensen et al., 2012; Noyes et al., 2008a), Bcd binds to the specific TAATCC motif (Bergman et al., 2005; Noyes et al., 2008a, Noyes et al., 2008b).
evidence: This is stated with citations to previous work.

claim: Including 7 bp of endogenous flanking sequence around each core Bcd motif dramatically increases the activity of a synthetic HbP2 enhancer.
source: This degree of specific binding makes it reasonable to assume that the core motif would be sufficient for Bcd binding and activity in vivo; however, here we show that including 7 bp of endogenous flanking sequence around each core Bcd motif dramatically increases the activity of a synthetic HbP2 enhancer.
evidence: This is an experimental observation from testing SynHbP2 variants.

claim: Increasing the flanking sequence to 12 bp did not result in any additional effect on SynHbP2 activity.
source: When we increased the flanking sequence to 12 bp, we didn't observe any additional effect.
evidence: This is an experimental observation from testing SynHbP2 variants.

claim: The flanking sequences around Bcd binding sites may form a specific DNA shape that is favorable for Bcd recognition.
source: We hypothesize that the flanks form a specific DNA shape that is favorable for Bcd recognition, as has been shown for other homeodomain proteins (Dror et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the experimental observations and cited work on other homeodomain proteins.

claim: Even after all six known binding sites are removed from WTHbP2, expression is still observed with a sigmoidal, non-linear response.
source: Even after all six known binding sites are removed from WTHbP2, we still observe gene expression with a sigmoidal, non-linear response.
evidence: This is an experimental observation from the binding site deletion series.

claim: WTHbP2 does not express at all when Bcd is removed by RNAi.
source: WTHbP2 does not express at all when Bcd is removed by RNAi (data not shown), indicating that some Bcd responsive element remains even after removing the canonical six sites.
evidence: This is an experimental observation from RNAi experiments.

claim: The WTHbP2 sequence contains one additional predicted Bcd binding site in addition to the canonical six which overlaps with a weak binding site.
source: The WTHbP2 sequence contains one additional predicted Bcd binding site in addition to the canonical six which overlaps with a weak binding site, and the native hb promoter also contains an additional predicted Bcd binding site.
evidence: This is a description of the sequence analysis.

claim: The native hb promoter contains an additional predicted Bcd binding site.
source: The WTHbP2 sequence contains one additional predicted Bcd binding site in addition to the canonical six which overlaps with a weak binding site, and the native hb promoter also contains an additional predicted Bcd binding site.
evidence: This is a description of the sequence analysis.

claim: Deleting two additional predicted Bcd sites further reduced gene expression but did not completely abolish it.
source: We deleted these two additional sites and measured expression; expression is lowered further but still detectable (see Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from additional binding site deletions.

claim: The conclusion that pairwise cooperative binding of Bcd is inadequate to produce the observed expression from HbP2 is unaffected by how many Bcd sites there are.
source: Importantly, our conclusion that pairwise cooperative binding of Bcd is inadequate to produce the observed expression from HbP2 is unaffected by how many Bcd sites there are (Estrada et al., 2016b).
evidence: This is a statement about the robustness of the study's conclusions with a citation to previous theoretical work.

claim: When considering the role of higher order cooperativity, additional binding sites allow the theory and experiment to be within range of one another.
source: However, when considering the role of higher order cooperativity, additional binding sites allow the theory and experiment to be within range of one another.
evidence: This is a conclusion from comparing experimental data to theoretical predictions.

claim: Multiple perturbations shifted the anterior/posterior location of expression driven by WTHbP2, reflecting a change in the sensitivity to Bcd concentration.
source: Multiple perturbations shifted the anterior/posterior location of expression driven by WTHbP2, reflecting a change in the sensitivity to Bcd concentration.
evidence: This summarizes experimental observations from various perturbations.

claim: The perturbations that shift expression location all influence the accessibility of WTHbP2, and thus the ability of Bcd to bind.
source: We hypothesize that these perturbations all influence the accessibility of WTHbP2, and thus the ability of Bcd to bind.
evidence: This is a hypothesis to explain the experimental observations.

claim: Removing binding sites for the pioneer factor Zelda may result in decreased accessibility of WTHbP2, a requirement for higher levels of Bcd to activate expression, and an anterior shift in expression.
source: For example, removing binding sites for the pioneer factor Zelda may result in decreased accessibility of WTHbP2, a requirement for higher levels of Bcd to activate expression, and an anterior shift in expression.
evidence: This is a mechanistic hypothesis to explain the experimental observations.

claim: Hb may facilitate Bcd binding through collaborative cooperativity.
source: Similarly, Hb may also facilitate Bcd binding through collaborative cooperativity, and CBP may be necessary to modify nucleosomes.
evidence: This is a mechanistic hypothesis to explain the experimental observations.

claim: CBP may be necessary to modify nucleosomes.
source: Similarly, Hb may also facilitate Bcd binding through collaborative cooperativity, and CBP may be necessary to modify nucleosomes.
evidence: This is a mechanistic hypothesis to explain the experimental observations.

claim: The hypothesis that perturbations influence WTHbP2 accessibility is consistent with previous studies where modulating Bcd concentrations influences the location of expression without altering the steepness.
source: This hypothesis is consistent with previous studies where modulating Bcd concentrations influences the location of expression without altering the steepness (Liu et al., 2013; Struhl et al., 1989).
evidence: This connects the current hypothesis to previous experimental findings with citations.

claim: Pairwise cooperative binding between TFs has been widely proposed to underlie sharp responses to graded inputs.
source: Specifically, pairwise cooperative binding between TFs has been widely proposed to underlie sharp responses to graded inputs (He et al., 2010b; Segal et al., 2008), though a series of models from the Reinitz group allow for higher-order cooperativity between TFs and other components (Reinitz et al., 2003; Janssens et al., 2006; Kim et al., 2013).
evidence: This describes a prevailing view in the field with citations.

claim: A series of models from the Reinitz group allow for higher-order cooperativity between TFs and other components.
source: Specifically, pairwise cooperative binding between TFs has been widely proposed to underlie sharp responses to graded inputs (He et al., 2010b; Segal et al., 2008), though a series of models from the Reinitz group allow for higher-order cooperativity between TFs and other components (Reinitz et al., 2003; Janssens et al., 2006; Kim et al., 2013).
evidence: This describes an alternative modeling approach with citations.

claim: The current study's work calls the TF-centric view into question using both theory and experiment.
source: Our work calls the TF-centric view into question using both theory and experiment.
evidence: This is a broad conclusion of the study.

claim: Theory grounded in physics must include higher order cooperativity between TFs to generate GRFs with sufficient steepness and position to compare to in vivo measurements.
source: We show that theory grounded in physics must include higher order cooperativity between TFs to generate GRFs with sufficient steepness and position to compare to in vivo measurements; this assumes that the regulatory mechanism is operating at thermodynamic equilibrium, which may still be inadequate to capture experimental data, indicating that energy dissipation may be required.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the theoretical analysis.

claim: The assumption that the regulatory mechanism is operating at thermodynamic equilibrium may be inadequate to capture experimental data, indicating that energy dissipation may be required.
source: We show that theory grounded in physics must include higher order cooperativity between TFs to generate GRFs with sufficient steepness and position to compare to in vivo measurements; this assumes that the regulatory mechanism is operating at thermodynamic equilibrium, which may still be inadequate to capture experimental data, indicating that energy dissipation may be required.
evidence: This is a conclusion from comparing theory to experimental data.

claim: Cofactors are prime candidates for implementing higher-order cooperativity or energy dissipation through binding directly to multiple TFs or by facilitating their binding through indirect processes such as chromatin remodeling or modification.
source: Cofactors are prime candidates for implementing higher-order cooperativity or energy dissipation through binding directly to multiple TFs or by facilitating their binding through indirect processes such as chromatin remodeling or modification.
evidence: This is a hypothesis about the role of cofactors based on the study's findings.

claim: A role for cofactors in shaping the GRF is consistent with in vitro studies where purified Bcd protein binds to HbP2 but yields a Hill coefficient of only 3–4.
source: A role for cofactors in shaping the GRF is consistent with in vitro studies where purified Bcd protein binds to HbP2 but yields a Hill coefficient of only 3–4 (Ma et al., 1996).
evidence: This connects the current findings to previous in vitro studies with a citation.

claim: Cofactors do not simply execute the decisions made by TFs; they collaborate with TFs to shape the quantitative features of the gene regulatory function.
source: Together, these results argue that cofactors do not simply execute the decisions made by TFs; they collaborate with TFs to shape the quantitative features of the gene regulatory function.
evidence: This is a broad conclusion of the study based on the experimental results.

claim: Cooperativity between TFs mediated by cofactors may help to explain the rapid evolution of regulatory DNA.
source: Cooperativity between TFs mediated by cofactors may help to explain the rapid evolution of regulatory DNA.
evidence: This is a speculative hypothesis about evolutionary implications.

claim: The number, position and affinity of WTHbP2 binding sites varies over evolutionary time.
source: Because cooperative binding requires direct TF-TF contact, it should be a strong constraint on regulatory evolution. However, the number, position and affinity of WTHbP2 binding sites varies over evolutionary time.
evidence: This is stated as an observation about evolutionary variation.

claim: Cooperativity through cofactors may enable rapid evolution of regulatory sequence as motifs at disparate locations can still be integrated into the output of the enhancer.
source: We speculate that cooperativity through cofactors may enable rapid evolution of regulatory sequence as motifs at disparate locations can still be integrated into the output of the enhancer.
evidence: This is a speculative hypothesis about evolutionary mechanisms.

claim: Coupling quantitative measurements to mechanistically meaningful biophysical models is a powerful strategy to decipher the individual role of molecular mechanisms in transcription.
source: Coupling quantitative measurements to mechanistically meaningful biophysical models is a powerful strategy to decipher the individual role of such mechanisms, and how they collaborate to influence gene expression.
evidence: This is a statement about the methodological approach of the study.

claim: This strategy has been enormously successful in bacteria.
source: This strategy has been enormously successful in bacteria (Belliveau et al., 2018; Landman et al., 2017; Razo-Mejia et al., 2018), and the toolbox for applying this strategy in animals is rapidly growing.
evidence: This is stated with citations to previous work in bacteria.

claim: Drosophila embryos are becoming a flagship system for coupling quantitative measurements to biophysical models due to key strengths developed by the community.
source: Drosophila embryos are becoming a flagship system for this strategy due to key strengths developed by the community over time: the transcriptional network is well studied (Levine, 2008; Nüsslein-Volhard and Wieschaus, 1980), high resolution imaging of mRNA and protein is tractable (Fowlkes et al., 2008; Gregor et al., 2014; Pisarev et al., 2009), and genetic and optogenetic perturbations are possible (Huang et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated with citations to previous work establishing these capabilities.

claim: Controlled synthetic systems will be a crucial tool to harness the molecular complexity of animal transcription.
source: Controlled synthetic systems, like the one we develop here and others that are emerging (Crocker et al., 2017), will be another crucial tool to harness the molecular complexity of animal transcription.
evidence: This is a statement about the value of synthetic systems with a citation to related work.

claim: Coupling measurements to models has the power to reveal fundamental features of transcription that differ between animals and bacteria.
source: As we show, coupling measurements to models has the power to reveal fundamental features of transcription that differ between animals and bacteria.
evidence: This is a broad conclusion about the methodological approach.

claim: As models improve, they will be a valuable tool in predicting the activity of animal enhancers and their variants and in engineering enhancers with desired activities.
source: As models improve, they will be a valuable tool in predicting the activity of animal enhancers and their variants and in engineering enhancers with desired activities, both of which are central goals of precision medicine.
evidence: This is a statement about future applications of the modeling approach.
